h1: The 8 Best Label Printers Under $100 for Shipping and Organizing, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Label Printers Under $100: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 8 label printers under $100, from Brother and DYMO label makers to Bluetooth thermal shipping printers, compared on use and cost.
summary: The Brother P-Touch PT-D610BT is the best label printer under $100 for offices and workshops, with Bluetooth connectivity and Brother's design options. The Phomemo Bluetooth shipping printer with USB is the best pick for online sellers, the SVANTTO prints at 180mm/s for busy shipping hours, and the DYMO LabelManager 160 is the simplest handheld.
intro: Anyone who buys a label printer without deciding what it will label ends up with the wrong machine. A handheld label maker prints narrow strips for shelves, cables and file folders. A thermal shipping printer prints large 4 by 6 inch labels for parcels. They solve different problems, they use different supplies, and they are not interchangeable. Choosing the type is the real decision, and the brand is secondary.

We ranked eight label printers under $100, three handheld label makers and five thermal printers for shipping. The thermal models share a common technology, which prints with heat and needs no ink, so their listings often read alike. We rank on connectivity, print speed, label compatibility and brand support, and flag where listings are thin.

products.name: Brother P-Touch PT-D610BT Business Professional Connected Label Maker with Bluetooth
products.verdict: A connected business label maker from the best-known brand in the category.
products.description:
The PT-D610BT is a Brother P-Touch business label maker with Bluetooth connectivity and Brother's design options for building labels. It falls in the $50 to $100 range and targets offices, workshops and regular organizing.

Brother tops the list because P-Touch tape is durable, widely stocked and available in many widths and finishes, and a Bluetooth link lets you design labels on a phone or computer rather than on a tiny keypad. For regular filing, equipment labeling and cable management, that matters more than raw speed. The cost of Brother is in tape, which is dearer than generic rolls.

Buy it for office and workshop labeling. Skip it for parcel shipping.
pros: Bluetooth design on phone or PC
products.skipIf: You ship parcels and need 4 by 6 inch labels.

products.name: Phomemo Bluetooth Shipping Label Printer
products.verdict: A Bluetooth and USB thermal shipping printer from a specialist in small label printers.
products.description:
This Phomemo printer is a thermal shipping label printer that connects wirelessly over Bluetooth and prints through a USB cable. It lists multi-platform compatibility and costs $50 to $100.

Where it lands, second, comes down to the fact that Phomemo is a specialist brand with a large following among marketplace sellers, and offering both Bluetooth and USB means it works with phones for travel and computers for batch printing. Thermal printing needs no ink, so running costs stay low. It does need thermal label rolls, and the listing gives no speed figure.

Buy it for an online store that ships daily. Check the supported label sizes before buying rolls.
pros: No ink needed for thermal labels
products.idealFor: Online sellers who ship every day.
products.skipIf: You label shelves and cables, not parcels.

products.name: SVANTTO Thermal Label Printer
products.verdict: A 180mm/s thermal printer with Bluetooth 4.0 and universal label compatibility.
products.description:
The SVANTTO prints at up to 180mm/s, uses Bluetooth 4.0 and advertises universal label compatibility with a label feeding function. It costs $50 to $100.

Speed is the reason for third place. At 180mm/s, a 4 by 6 inch label comes out in about a second, which matters when you print dozens during a rush. Universal label compatibility means you are not locked to one brand of roll, which saves money. Bluetooth 4.0 is an older standard, so connection stability may lag newer versions.

Buy it if print speed matters for volume. The Phomemo with USB is steadier for desktops.
products.idealFor: Busy sellers who print many labels quickly.
products.skipIf: You want a USB-first desktop printer.

products.name: Nelko Bluetooth Thermal Shipping Label Printer
products.verdict: A Bluetooth and USB thermal printer pitched at cutting shipping label costs.
products.description:
The Nelko is a thermal shipping label printer that prints wirelessly by Bluetooth or through a USB cable, and the listing calls it a helper for saving money. It costs $50 to $100.

The fourth spot follows because it matches the Phomemo on connections and pitches itself on cost, since printing your own labels avoids paying for pre-printed ones. The listing has fewer details on speed or label support than the SVANTTO, and Nelko is a smaller name.

Buy it if you want a simple, low-cost shipping printer. Compare it with the Phomemo before ordering.
products.idealFor: Small sellers looking to cut shipping costs.
products.skipIf: You want a stated print speed.

products.name: Thermal Shipping Label Printer 4x6 Bluetooth Label Maker for Small Business
products.verdict: A 4x6 thermal printer with Bluetooth and USB, aimed at small businesses.
products.description:
This printer prints 4x6 thermal labels, connects by Bluetooth and USB, and is described as energy-efficient and user-friendly. It costs $50 to $100 and targets small businesses.

Its fifth position rests on how the listing is generic, with no brand name and no stated speed. The dual connection is welcome, and 4x6 is the standard parcel label size. Support is uncertain with an unbranded product, so keep the return window in mind.

Buy it if you want a cheap, standard 4x6 printer. A named brand is safer.
products.idealFor: Small businesses wanting a basic 4x6 printer.

products.name: NIIMBOT M2 Label Maker with Tape 2Inch Thermal Transfer Label Printer
products.verdict: A 2 inch thermal transfer label maker with mobile and PC editing.
products.description:
The NIIMBOT M2 is a compact 2 inch label maker that uses thermal transfer technology, includes tape and edits from mobile or PC. It costs $50 to $100.

Thermal transfer uses a ribbon, which makes prints more durable than direct thermal, so labels resist fading better. A 2 inch width suits product labels, jars and small parcels, though not full 4x6 shipping labels. It ranks sixth because it sits between the handheld and shipping classes, and the supplies are less widely stocked than Brother's.

Buy it for product and shelf labels with a phone-friendly design app. Not for parcel shipping.

products.name: DYMO LabelManager 160 Label Maker Bundle with 3 D1 Label Cassettes
products.verdict: A compact, portable handheld with three D1 cassettes in the bundle.
products.description:
The DYMO LabelManager 160 is a compact, portable label maker with customizable labels, supplied in a bundle with three D1 label cassettes. It costs $50 to $100.

It places seventh because it is a plain keypad machine without Bluetooth, so you type labels on the device. For quick household and office jobs, that simplicity is a plus. The three included cassettes give you a head start on supplies, and D1 tape is easy to find.

Buy it for simple labeling around the home. Choose the Brother if you want phone design.
products.skipIf: You want to design labels on your phone.

products.name: Phomemo Bluetooth Thermal Shipping Label Printer
products.verdict: A Phomemo Bluetooth thermal printer for commercial and home use.
products.description:
This Phomemo printer prints shipping labels via Bluetooth, supports multiple platforms and is marketed for commercial and home use. It costs $50 to $100.

Rank eighth is a result of the fact that the listing mentions Bluetooth only and offers less than the other Phomemo with USB. It is still a capable thermal shipping printer and benefits from the Phomemo brand's following, but the stronger sibling is a better pick at the same tier.

Buy it if you prefer a wireless-only setup. Choose the USB model for desktops.
products.skipIf: You want USB for a desktop.

whatMatters.detail: A handheld label maker prints narrow tapes for shelves, cables and files, while a thermal shipping printer prints 4 by 6 inch labels for parcels. Choose by the job. Using the wrong one wastes money and supplies.

Direct thermal printers use heat on special paper and need no ink or toner. This keeps costs low, but the labels fade with sun and heat over time. Thermal transfer uses a ribbon for more durable prints.
Bluetooth lets you print from a phone, while USB suits a desktop and avoids pairing problems. Dual connectivity is the most flexible. Check that your computer's operating system is supported.
Speed is quoted in millimeters per second. At 180mm/s, a 4 by 6 inch label prints in about a second, which helps when you ship in volume. For occasional use, speed matters little.
Brother and DYMO tapes are easy to find but pricier, while thermal rolls are cheap and ink-free. Check that the printer accepts third-party labels. Count the cost of rolls or tape over a year.

howToChoose.intro: Start with what you will label, since that decides the whole category.

cards.label: Handheld label maker
cards.text: Prints narrow strips for shelves, cables and files. The Brother PT-D610BT, DYMO LabelManager 160 and NIIMBOT M2 are examples.

cards.label: Thermal shipping printer
cards.text: Prints 4 by 6 inch labels for parcels with no ink. The Phomemo, Nelko, SVANTTO and generic 4x6 printer are for this.

howToChoose.note: Choose a handheld for organizing and a thermal shipping printer for parcels, since neither does the other's job well.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: 4 by 6 inch thermal support, USB for a desktop and Bluetooth for a phone, plus universal label rolls to keep supply costs low.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: The Phomemo with Bluetooth and USB is the best choice, and the SVANTTO is the speed pick for busy hours.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You label daily for an office or workshop. The Brother P-Touch PT-D610BT is built for it and has widely available tape.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You label occasionally. The DYMO LabelManager 160 and the unbranded 4x6 printer cover the basics.

faq.q: Will these printers work with Etsy, eBay or Amazon?
faq.a: Thermal shipping printers generally print 4 by 6 inch labels from those platforms through a PDF. Check that the printer lists the platforms you use. The Phomemo lists multi-platform compatibility.

faq.q: What is the common mistake buying a label printer?
faq.a: Buying a handheld for shipping, or a shipping printer for shelves. They use different label sizes. Decide the job first.

faq.q: Is a Brother worth it over a cheaper thermal printer?
faq.a: For office labeling, yes. Brother tape is durable and widely sold. Thermal shipping printers cost less per label but are not designed for narrow labels.

faq.q: How do I load the label roll?
faq.a: Open the lid, place the roll or cassette so the labels feed from the correct side, and close the lid. Feed a label to align. Check the manual for sensor calibration.
Direct thermal labels can fade with heat, sunlight and time. For long-term labels, choose thermal transfer like the NIIMBOT. For parcels, fading is rarely a concern.
The SVANTTO advertises universal compatibility. Others may accept third-party rolls of the right size. Brother and DYMO prefer their own cassettes.

finalTake: The Brother P-Touch PT-D610BT is the best label printer under $100 for offices and workshops, with Bluetooth design and reliable tape. Online sellers should choose the Phomemo with Bluetooth and USB, or the SVANTTO for speed. The DYMO LabelManager 160 and NIIMBOT M2 cover simple and compact jobs.
